summary_en: This study tests lenvatinib and pembrolizumab with a short course of pelvic radiation therapy in people with recurrent or unresectable endometrial carcinoma that is mismatch repair proficient (pMMR). Lenvatinib is taken by mouth every day at dose levels of 4, 8, 12 or 16 mg, pembrolizumab 200 mg is given through a vein on Days 1, 22 and 43, and whole pelvic radiation is given in 16 daily-fraction doses of 2.5 Gy (40 Gy) followed by a boost, with about 7 weeks of radiation and about 10 to 12 weeks of total treatment. The study is a Phase 1 trial that aims to see whether this combination is feasible, and no main outcome measure is listed in the record.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa lenvatinib y pembrolizumab junto con un curso corto de radioterapia pélvica en personas con carcinoma endometrial recurrente o no operable que es pMMR (con reparación de desajustes competente). El lenvatinib se toma por vía oral todos los días en dosis de 4, 8, 12 o 16 mg, el pembrolizumab de 200 mg se aplica por vía intravenosa los días 1, 22 y 43, y la radioterapia pélvica total se administra en 16 fracciones de 2,5 Gy (40 Gy) seguidas de un refuerzo, con unas 7 semanas de radiación y unas 10 a 12 semanas de tratamiento total. Es un estudio de fase 1 que busca determinar si esta combinación es factible, y el registro no indica una medida de resultado principal.
who_for: Biopsy-proven recurrent or unresectable pMMR endometrial carcinoma, or uterine carcinosarcoma, for whom external beam radiation is considered appropriate.
Measurable disease of at least 1.0 cm, with at least one site in the pelvis or vagina and no disease outside the pelvis.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2 (Karnofsky score 50 or higher).
Adequate blood counts, kidney, liver and albumin levels as defined in the record.
Age 18 or older, able to sign consent, and using birth control if of childbearing potential.
not_for: Mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) endometrial carcinoma or dMMR uterine carcinosarcoma.
Known active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
Prior external beam radiation to the vagina, pelvis or abdomen.
Another malignancy that is progressing or needs active treatment (some skin cancers and in situ cervical cancer excepted).
Investigational agent within 4 weeks, or systemic steroids or immunosuppressive therapy within 21 days before the first dose.
